event: Pip chimes twice, a sharp staccato warning Callum has never heard before.
Compound Growth is climbing back, 9.4%, 9.7%, the feedback tighter since the Script Engine upgrade.
Pip's status: external approach, single entity, threat indeterminate. "Jin. Wake up."
Jin sits up from beside Chunk; Pixel chirps confirmation, and Jin brings Zephyr from standby.
Loop Analysis finds one contact: no constructs, no squad, and a power reading of Level 40-plus.
Mira is already at the loading door, hand on her hilt; her Danger Sense heard Pip's threat first.
A tall man walks up the access road alone, grey at the temples, in scarred Commander plate.
Insignia display off, no entourage, a greatsword across his back: Drake Morrison.
"He's alone." "I noticed." "That's either very good or very bad."
Drake nods to Mira, fighter to fighter: he's here to talk to her builder, not to fight.
"You brought a sword." "I always bring a sword. So do you." She steps aside, not far.
Drake walks the array without a word, and stands a long time watching the Enhancement Construct.
His output doubled five times in two weeks, Drake says, flagged by Bray. "And you're Level 20."
"Twenty-two." Two level-ups that morning, their points dumped into Intelligence and Wisdom.

event: Drake has been Level 42 for three weeks; the curve past forty is a cliff.
Last Tuesday he killed a six-legged Fracture boss; it took forty minutes and three potions.
An engineer with four constructs will out-earn him by doing nothing. "Automation." "Same thing."
His people pulled the class registry: one Loopweaver in the world, and he's in Drake's zone.
"I'm not here because I'm angry. I'm here because I'm scared."
Scared of the next surge, with the Barrier resting on someone who has never really fought.
He has buried sixty-three people, forty-one in the first month, and keeps their names in a journal.
If the machines crash, who fights? "You? With your fifteen Strength?" Callum says nothing.
He offers a choice. One: join the Vanguard, protected, with forty percent of his output to it.
Everyone's constrained, Drake says: by people who want you alive, or by a surge that doesn't care.
Two: cease independent construct operations and contribute through official channels.
He pays his Residuum, Callum says. The minimum, says Drake, of ten times what he could.
Neither? Then Drake can't guarantee his zone access continues. Not a threat; a fact.
Callum: Drake is hitting a wall while wave intensity rises five percent a month. Exponential.
"I'm not your enemy. I'm the only thing in this zone scaling fast enough to match what's coming."
Something load-bearing in Drake cracks; he holds up hands mapped with burns and scars.
Every scar is a monster that didn't reach the Barrier. Power not earned can't be trusted.
"It cares about throughput," Callum says. "Then the Substrate is wrong," says Drake.
It is belief built on graves: Marcus Morrison died on Day Three, holding a line at I-94.
Mathematically wrong, Callum knows; but not morally wrong, and he has no answer to it.
He lost seven coworkers on Day One, hiding nine hours in a hydraulic press. He knows the cost.
Drake nods once: acknowledgment, not agreement. "Think about it. You have a week."
At the door: things that don't bleed don't fight hard enough when it matters. He goes.
Mira doesn't relax until his footsteps pass beyond the reach of her Danger Sense.
Jin: his scout read Drake like the sun through a pinhole. Strength 98, 1,338 HP, Callum says.
Join, cease, or lose the zones: every option fails. There is a fourth: Condense.
"I'm going to Condense." His voice is flat; his hands are not steady, and Pip flickers fast.
Level 1, Mira says: anything in this zone that kills a Level 20 kills him in one hit.
"That's why I need you. Both of you. While I'm weak."
Jin balks; Callum has the curve: with 1.5x, nine days back to 25, then Condense again.
"Stop mathing and listen to me." Nine days where anyone can walk in and push, Mira says.
"Is it insane if the math works?" "Math doesn't stop a sword." "No. That's what you're for."
"Okay," Mira says: the hard kind of trust. But a plan, fallbacks, and if he's off by a day...
She'll drag him to the Barrier by his collar. "My math isn't wrong." "It better not be."
Jin, hands shaking: the first compound-prestige attempt in Detroit? "Obviously I'm in."
A sword saint and a sophomore with a calculator talisman: for a moment all that's left is gratitude.
"First," he says, "we level."
Three skill points take Compile Familiar to 3: a status display, and Pip runs one thread alone.
"Hey. You in there?" Pip chimes, warm as a struck tuning fork. "Good. We're going to need you."
Thirty-one hours after the reset, Compound Growth is at 11.2%, and the push begins.
A nineteen-line rewrite on Script Engine 5 gives the Sentinel eight percent more kill speed.
Chunk and Zephyr fight beside the Sentinel in the Flats, clearing spawns forty percent faster.
Mira runs the Overgrowth on foot twelve hours a day, front-loading the danger.
Level up, 22 to 23: Intelligence 72, Wisdom 75, Willpower 39. He banks the skill points.

changes.note: Level 22 to 23 during the forty-eight-hour push

event: Each level is a step closer to 25, and the choice that waits there.
Fourteen hours later: 23 to 24. Intelligence 74, Wisdom 77; Compound Growth +27.8%.
About 14,200 Essence a day. HP 410, MP 1,007, Complexity 42, Idle Yield 2.54x.
Numbers fit for a Level 40 mage, in a body that couldn't outrun a moderately annoyed dog.
Condense threshold approaching: about 42 Prestige Shards, a projected 1.5x. This cannot be reversed.
The Substrate never warns; here it does. He dismisses it and lies back.
One more level, tomorrow or the day after. Then 410 HP becomes 151.
But the multiplier, his mind whispers: nine days back to 25, and faster every cycle after.
He thinks of Drake's scarred hands, Mira's "Okay," and seven coworkers dying behind sheet metal.
Pip's glow makes a small gold circle on the wall. "One more level." Pip chimes, soft and sure.
He doesn't sleep; he watches the numbers climb behind his eyelids. This time, everyone is watching.
